Rate_Capability.source_text: LiLCO cells with various electrolytes deliver similar specific discharge capacity in the first 20 cycles, after which the cells with base and PB electrolytes drastically drop below 100 mAh g⁻¹ when the current density is enhanced to 1.5 C, and severe deterioration occurs when the current density is further increased to 2 C. In contrast, cells with PN and PBN electrolytes maintain apparently higher capacities of 139.3 and 159.3 mAh g⁻¹ at 1.5 C, and the capacity moderately drops to 118.2 and 137.2 mAh g⁻¹ after raising the current density to 2 C. When the current density is set back to 0.2 C, cells with PN and PBN electrolytes still remain high capacities of 163.2 and 150.1 mA h g⁻¹, which is superior to the cells with the base electrolyte 123.3 mAh g⁻¹ and PB electrolyte 128.4 mAh g⁻¹. Similar results are observed for LiNCM811 cells. The cells with PN and PBN electrolytes exhibit large discharge capacities of 107.0 and 120.3 mAh g⁻¹ at 2 C, which are apparently higher than that of PB electrolyte of 45.9 mA h g⁻¹ and base electrolyte of 35.2 mAh g⁻¹.
